target_name: Industry Relative Reinvestment Within Cheap Half
rationale: This is the archive's best signal ("Capital Discipline Within Cheap Firms") with two normalization tweaks — the gate moved from the top 30% to the top 50% and ZSCORE replaced by IND_ZSCORE — which is close to the cosmetic re-parameterization the objective warns against rather than a substantively new mechanism.

target_name: Capacity Expansion Within Cheap EBITDA Yield Half
rationale: The cheapness × gross-capacity-growth interaction was already tested in the archive ("Value Premium Flip Across Capacity Growth Regimes") and produced a wrong-signed FMB t-stat of −2.52, so re-running essentially the same economic content in gated form with an EBITDA-yield gate is a rediscovery with prior evidence against it, and the investment leg is little more than the published asset-growth anomaly inside value stocks.

target_name: Equity Funded Expansion Within Cheap Half
rationale: Long cheap/low-issuance versus cheap/high-issuance is a direct restatement of the well-published equity-issuance anomaly crossed with value, and it re-uses the exact funding variable from the gen-0 archive signal, so the only genuine novelty is the container rather than the information.

target_name: Acquired Goodwill Growth Within Cheap Half
rationale: The inorganic-investment dimension is a legitimately different channel from capex, but DELTA(gdwl) conflates acquisitions with goodwill impairments, so the long leg deliberately buys cheap firms writing off goodwill — bad news that plausibly predicts low, not high, returns — and separately-reported goodwill is largely a post-SFAS-142 item, risking a regime-driven coverage break.

target_name: Working Capital Buildup Weighted By Sales Yield
rationale: Inventory-growth-relative-to-sales is close to the published inventory-change anomaly, but the working-capital channel plus a continuous bounded cheapness weight is a defensibly different test of whether the archive's alpha comes from conditioning shape or content — the main hazard is that GROWTH(invt/sale) is degenerate for low- or zero-inventory firms and will skew coverage toward manufacturers.

A second moment of investment is the batch's only genuinely new dimension and is not spanned by CMA, but VOL of capx/ppent over only three observations is a very noisy estimate whose magnitude scales mechanically with the mean reinvestment rate, so the result must be checked against the archive winner's level signal to confirm it is not just a degraded proxy for it.
